# E4g — what each phase is bound by (C1), and what the best rung fixed (C2)

**Generated by `bench/analyze_c1.py` from the ncu CSVs.** Nothing is typed in. Each capture is one (model, mode, phase): 40 kernel launches with SpeedOfLight, MemoryWorkloadAnalysis, WarpStateStats and Occupancy, plus the 14 `smsp__average_warps_issue_stalled_*` metrics requested by name.

Per-kernel numbers are averaged **weighted by kernel duration**; an unweighted mean lets a 2 µs elementwise kernel count as much as a 234 µs convolution. The bound/unbound thresholds are ncu's own SOLBottleneck rule (80 % of SM or memory throughput), not values chosen here: at or above 80 % the phase is bound by whichever is higher, below 60 % on both it is latency bound and the dominant stall names which latency.

## C2 — eager → best, phase by phase

**`best` here is LeRobot's own compiled path** (`compile_model=True`, `reduce-overhead`), which compiles `sample_actions` as one unit — the ladder's `whole_graphs` rung. A consequence worth stating: per-phase wall times do not exist for that configuration, because a region boundary cannot be placed inside a single compiled graph. **So this table reports no speedup.** Phase wall times, and the speedups that go with them, are in `reports/E4d_phase_balance.md`, measured on the ladder rungs that keep their regions.

What is compared here are the ncu counters, which are intensive quantities describing what the kernels in a phase are doing — those do compare across modes. Summed captured duration does not: `-c 40` takes the first 40 kernels of a range and the kernel mix differs between modes, which is how an earlier version of this table showed π0's `vlm_prefix` at "0.11×" while Part B measured 234 → 195 ms.

## C3 — the action expert's operand dimensions

Read from each checkpoint's own tensor shapes (every GR00T checkpoint is sharded, so the reader follows the shard index; the first shard alone would miss most of the action head). `S` is the suffix length, **measured** on a real inference rather than taken from `chunk_size`/`action_horizon` — π0's `chunk_size` is 50 while its measured S is 51, because a state token is prepended.

| model | expert layers | projections/layer | GEMMs | S | I ≈ S (FLOP/B) | vs measured ridge 180.57 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| pi0 | 18 | 7 | 126 | 51 | 51 | MEMORY-bound by construction (S < ridge) |
| pi05 | 18 | 9 | 162 | 50 | 50 | MEMORY-bound by construction (S < ridge) |
| smolvla | 16 | 7 | 112 | 50 | 50 | MEMORY-bound by construction (S < ridge) |
| groot_n17 | 32 | 7 | 224 | 41 | 41 | MEMORY-bound by construction (S < ridge) |
| groot_n16 | 32 | 7 | 224 | 51 | 51 | MEMORY-bound by construction (S < ridge) |
| groot_n15 | 16 | 7 | 112 | 49 | 49 | MEMORY-bound by construction (S < ridge) |

The skinniest GEMM in each expert — the long-shallow shape the owner predicted:

| model | projection | A (activations) | B (weights) | K/M | I |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| pi0 | `mlp.down_proj` | [51 x 4096] | [4096 x 1024] | 80.3 | 48.0 |
| pi05 | `mlp.down_proj` | [50 x 4096] | [4096 x 1024] | 81.9 | 47.1 |
| smolvla | `mlp.down_proj` | [50 x 2048] | [2048 x 720] | 41.0 | 45.7 |
| groot_n17 | `ff.net.2` | [41 x 6144] | [6144 x 1536] | 149.9 | 39.7 |
| groot_n16 | `ff.net.2` | [51 x 6144] | [6144 x 1536] | 120.5 | 49.0 |
| groot_n15 | `ff.net.2` | [49 x 6144] | [6144 x 1536] | 125.4 | 47.1 |

**The analytic verdict and the measured one disagree, and that is the point.** I ≈ S puts every expert GEMM far below the measured ridge, so analytically they are all memory-bound by construction. C1's counters say π0's expert is *issue*-limited when eager (`imc_miss` 35 %, Long Scoreboard third at 16 %, memory throughput 21.6 %) and only becomes memory-latency-bound once compiled (56.5 %, Long Scoreboard dominant). Arithmetic intensity bounds what a phase *could* achieve; it does not say what limits it now.

Captures summarised: **36**. A phase missing from a table has no usable capture yet — `bench/c1_capture_ok.py` rejects any CSV without all 14 stall metrics, so a partial capture is never silently averaged in.
